scope: Literature-focused mechanism review; no new original simulation or hypothesis-testing calculation added.
structure: Network connectivity and turnover link force generation to dissipation.
Transport, local RhoA feedback and mechanochemical aggregation are compared with their respective experimental constraints.
Flow-induced actin alignment, PAR redistribution and chiral torque remain distinct mechanisms.
Cortex-to-cytoplasm and cortex-to-junction transmission are compared through published spatial and paired-motion evidence.
Ingression, enclosure, anisotropic epidermal loading and material renewal connect subcellular processes to embryonic shape; full tissue models are linked to note 06.

evidence_changes.role: Place the experimentally constrained local feedback model beside AB-cell pulse measurements; do not infer spatial wave propagation from the local ODE.
Place transport-corrected reaction analysis and the published mechanochemical model together; identify the single-field growth rate as an explanatory reduction.
Connect measured velocity and compression to fitted orientation profiles, perturbations and ingression theory.
Use original 3D flow and PIV profiles as evidence; keep the analytic ellipse as a small principle illustration.
Pair observed slippage, measurement workflow and zyxin perturbation; identify the spring-network illustration as distinct from a fit to these experiments.

evidence_changes.paper: Lardennois et al. 2019 and Yang et al. 2025
evidence_changes.role: Reuse original network-remodeling and junction-exchange figures instead of scalar cylinder demonstrations.

archival_policy: The three withdrawn self-authored example assets and both Dai paper figures remain in the shared library. Other notes retain their figures and locations.
